newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: New Pakistani cabinet slashes own salaries in half.
newsitem.headline: New Pakistani cabinet slashes own salaries in half.

text.p: Pakistan's two-day-old caretaker government cut minister's salaries in half on Wednesday as part of an austerity package aimed at trimming spending and checking the "VIP culture".
Information Minister Irshaad Haqqani said interim Prime Minister Meraj Khalid's cabinet adopted the belt-tightening measures at its first meeting, one day after taking office.
"The cabinet members decided to voluntarily have their salaries reduced by 50 percent," Haqqani told a news conference.
The salary cut was part of a broader package which Haqqani said aimed at "cutting down expenditure on the maintenance of cabinet ministers and check the growing tendency of VIP culture".

He said use of cars by cabinet members is to be curtailed and ministers are barred from travelling by first class or seeking medical treatment abroad at government expense. The cabinet also decided to abolish VIP lounges at airports.
"The cabinet noted that the use of VIP lounges at airports has become a measure of class status which is an anachronism in an Islamic and democratic order," he said.

Haqqani said Khalid, who took over after former Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto was sacked by President Farooq Leghari on Tuesday, acknowledged it would be difficult for an interim government to substantially improve the country's economic situation.
"With proper management and an imaginative approach, it should be possible to provide some relief to the people groaning under unbearable economic hardships," Haqqani said.
Leghari accused Bhutto's government of corruption, nepotism and misrule. He has set general elections for February 3.
Noting widespread allegations of corruption, the caretaker cabinet appealed to citizens to send evidence of such misdeeds to the interior minister to aid in the fight against graft.
Khalid also told the cabinet that Pakistan's foreign policy objectives would remain unchanged, Haqqani said.

"Pakistan would continue to seek peace with all with enmity towards none. Pakistan would neither interfere in the internal affairs of any country nor would it tolerate interference by any power, big or small," Haqqani quoted Khalid as saying.
